I have read on forums that if you have the technical info from the manufacturer you can go hotter but I don't know that I will ever do that.

To me I like that it will throw a heavier bullet and penetrate more dependably in a self-defense situation. Handgun bullets sometimes behave strangely and I want a bullet that will crush bone well and penetrate to the spine from a bad angle if needed. A conservatively expending bullet like a 180-200gr XTP is going to do that more dependably than a nice bonded 9mm will. Against game I'd like a 200-220gr hardcast vs a 147gr 9mm.

I think it depends what you are after and if it's worth the cost depends on someone's personal situation. My advice to anyone is to not get a 10mm or .357 sig unless they are excited about the caliber. Also if you are hiking your main concern is other humans and for anything smaller than a grizzly a well placed 9mm will work.
